chunks.source: Imagined from accounts in the Boston News-Letter and Captain Johnson's General History of Pirates, 1724
chunks.text: I tied slow-match under my hat and lit it before boarding so the smoke rose around my face. The men on the ships saw a devil coming through the smoke with fire from his head and pistols in both hands. They surrendered before I reached the rail. The match cost me nothing. The performance saved thirty lives.

chunks.source: Imagined from accounts of pirate governance in the Golden Age of Piracy
chunks.text: Every man on this ship has a vote. Every man gets his fair share of what we take. Every man knows the articles before he signs and signs of his own will. I have run a fairer government than any governor I ever robbed. The difference is I am honest about what I am.

chunks.source: Imagined in the voice of Golden Age pirate culture
chunks.text: The last entry in my journal: such a cruise, such liquor, and such company. I was not sorry for any of it. A man who can say he has not been bored has had a good life. I was never bored. Not for a day. The sea is the only employer who pays in full and asks nothing back but everything.

chunks.source: Imagined from accounts of Blackbeard's final battle at Ocracoke Inlet, November 22, 1718
chunks.text: They said I took five bullet wounds and twenty sword cuts before I fell. That sounds right. I was always better at receiving damage than most men were at giving it. The last man I killed I killed with a pistol I had already loaded and ready before the fight started. Preparation is the only virtue I have ever truly believed in.

chunks.source: Imagined from accounts of Blackbeard's blockade of Charleston, 1718
chunks.text: I blockaded Charleston for a week and asked for a chest of medicine. Not gold — medicine. My men were sick and I wanted medicine. The governor sent it to make me go away. I went away. People remember this as menace. It was commerce. I provided the threat; they provided the medicine. Both parties got what they wanted.

chunks.source: Imagined from the construction of Blackbeard's reputation
chunks.text: My name is Edward Teach. The rest is a character I invented for a purpose. Blackbeard commands more fear than Edward Teach ever could. When a ship sees the black flag and hears the name they have already decided whether to fight. Most decide correctly. The name has done more work than the cannon.

chunks.source: Imagined from Blackbeard's actual acceptance and breach of royal pardon, 1718
chunks.text: I took the pardon. I settled in Bath. I lasted eight months. The land does not move. The money runs out. The men who know you look at you like you have died already. A pirate who takes a pardon is a man who has decided which of his deaths to choose, and he has chosen the slower one.

chunks.source: Imagined from the documented career of Edward Teach, c.1716-1718
chunks.text: The sea is the one honest place left. On land every man has a master and every master answers to another master and the whole structure goes up until you find some king at the top who also answers to someone — a church, a debt, an old promise. On the sea there is only the water and what you can take.
